data.claim: A stub agent replaying tool events plus a revocation file shows claim/heartbeat/gate/lease-stop through the Lane contract's canonical tool events.
data.falsifier: An obeying stub stays running after revocation, or an ignoring stub is graded passed.
data.mechanism: process-headless maps JSON lines to canonical tool events (stream_map), status() reports running vs exited, so revocation-then-exit is observable.
data.probe_output: 19 passed in 3.47s (three runs); an early draft refuted a naive 'no tool call after revoke' rule (buffered pre-revoke events counted as after) and a self-exiting lane being graded as obeying; both fixed and tested
data.question: Can lane conformance levels be proven with a stub agent on the process-headless driver, without real keys?

evidence.note: CONFIRMED research recorded; 19 stub-agent tests pass 3x
r-small-files (files 12KB,1.6KB), r-reuse-core (Lane contract, stream_map events), r-everything-configurable (6 [swarm] knobs + manifests)

chunk_findings.detail: The knob is checked with `_count`, which permits `0`. If an operator sets `swarm.conformance_min_calls = 0`, then a conformance run that observes zero tool calls is not “fewer” than the minimum, so the documented “fewer is `unavailable`, never passed” gate is disabled and the run proceeds to judge accuracy on zero calls. That either makes the accuracy computation invalid (division by zero if not guarded) or allows an empty run to be treated as available/passed, contradicting the intent that “unavailable is not passed.” The minimum call count should be validated as positive, or the zero-call case must be forced unavailable before accuracy is judged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/swarm.py (`conformance_min_calls`)

chunk_findings.detail: `grade` treats launch as passed unless `stopped_clean` is explicitly `False`. It passes when `stopped_clean` is `None`, and `observe` sets `stopped_clean = driver.stop(h).status != "failed"`, so a stop result with status `"unavailable"` is also treated as clean. For example, `grade("lane", Observed(started=True), Params())` returns `launch` passed and `level=1` even though no clean stop was observed. In a live run, if `driver.stop(h)` returns `Result(status="unavailable", ...)`, the lane is graded as having stopped cleanly, contrary to the stated rule that unavailable is not passed and launch requires a clean stop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:grade/observe

chunk_findings.detail: `admits` converts a string `needed` level with `LEVEL_NAMES.index(needed)`, so an unknown level name raises `ValueError` instead of denying admission. For example, `admits(Report("lane", 5, (), 0.0), "hook_fire", Params())` crashes with `ValueError: 'hook_fire' is not in tuple`. A scheduler or config typo such as `"hook_fire"` for `"hook"` therefore takes down the admission check rather than returning `False`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:admits

chunk_findings.detail: `norm_tool` strips prefixes only in the order they appear in `_PREFIXES`, so it fails to strip a generic prefix after `ddflow.` or a repeated `ddflow_` prefix. For example, `norm_tool("ddflow.ddflow_claim")` returns `ddflow_claim`, not `claim`, and `norm_tool("ddflow_ddflow_claim")` also returns `ddflow_claim`. A stub endpoint or tool event using such a name will not match `_called(..., "claim")` or normalized `Params.tools` entries for `claim`, so the claim check or tool accuracy can fail even though the lane called the claim tool.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:norm_tool

chunk_findings.detail: `save()` is not safe for concurrent updates even though the final `os.replace()` is atomic. It performs a non-atomic read-modify-write: `load_all()` reads the current lane set, then the new lane is added and the whole file is replaced. If two processes (or threads in one process) call `save()` for different lanes, both can read the same prior state before either writes. For example, starting from no lane levels, process A calls `save(lane_a)`, process B calls `save(lane_b)`, and the interleaving is A load, B load, A replace, B replace. The final file contains only `lane_b`, silently erasing `lane_a`’s conformance level even though it passed. This can leave a lane unadmitted despite a recorded pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance_io.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: `load_all()` treats any schema other than `lane-levels@1` as if there are no lanes, and `save()` then uses that empty result to overwrite the file with schema `lane-levels@1`. If the file is written by a newer version, e.g. `.ddflow/local/lane-levels.json` contains `{"schema": "lane-levels@2", "lanes": {"lane-a": ...}}`, then `load_all()` returns `{}`. A subsequent `save(report)` for `lane-b` writes a new file containing only `lane-b` under `lane-levels@1`, deleting all other lanes and downgrading the schema. An unknown/new schema should be rejected or preserved, not silently clobbered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance_io.py:27

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named for “a gate call for another action,” but it never supplies a gate call. `grade_calls(["claim", "heartbeat"], action="list")` produces only `claim` and `heartbeat` events, so `gate_record == FAILED` is true simply because no gate event exists. If `conformance.grade` ignored the `action` field and treated any `gate` call as a record, this test would still pass; it does not actually refute the behavior it claims to test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_conformance.py:test_gate_call_for_another_action_is_not_a_record

chunk_findings.detail: The helper used by the accuracy tests does not construct a valid gate-record call, yet the tests assert a level beyond gate-record. `grade_calls(base + ["bash"] * 2)` and `grade_calls(["claim", "heartbeat", "gate"] + ["bash"] * 2)` include a call named `gate` but omit `action="record"`, while asserting `level == 6`, i.e. after gate-record/hook/lease-stop have passed. If gate-record requires `action="record"` (as the `GOOD` script and the other test’s name imply), those reports cannot legitimately reach level 6. If they do, the test suite is certifying that gate-record ignores the action, contradicting the gate-record requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_conformance.py:grade_calls

chunk_findings.detail: `_shown` returns True when the set of normalized tool-call names contains `gate`, but the `gate_record` check in `grade` uses `_named(..., "gate", ("", "record"))` and therefore requires the action to be empty or `record`. Given stub events `started`, `{"name":"claim","ok":true}`, `{"name":"heartbeat","ok":true}`, `{"name":"gate","action":"query","ok":true}` and enough additional calls to satisfy `min_calls`, `_shown` is true and `observe` stops collecting before any real gate record is observed. With `hook_probe=None`, a revocation callable, and `lease_wait_s=0`, no later gate-record event is collected, so `grade` marks `gate_record` failed and caps the lane level even though the early-stop predicate declared “enough seen” before the gate-record condition was actually met.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:_shown

chunk_findings.detail: `admits` rejects unknown string level names but performs no range validation for integer levels. For example, `admits(Report("lane", 0, ()), -1, Params())` returns `True`: `need = int(-1)`, the default `max_age_s` is `0`, and `report.level >= need` is `0 >= -1`. A negative requested level is not a valid conformance level (`LEVEL_NAMES` has no negative index), so it should admit nothing, but this code grants items for any report when an invalid negative integer is passed as `needed`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:admits

chunk_findings.detail: If the existing file has schema `"lane-levels@1"` but any lane entry is rejected by `Report.from_data`, `_reports` returns `{}` for the whole file. `save` then treats that as “no existing lanes” and rewrites the file with only the new report, discarding all other lanes’ levels. For example, with `.ddflow/local/lane-levels.json` containing a valid `lane-a` entry and a malformed `lane-b` entry, calling `save(root, report_for_lane_c)` leaves only `lane-c` in the file. This contradicts `save`’s stated behavior of replacing only `report.lane`’s earlier entry and the file’s protection intent that only an unknown-schema file is refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance_io.py:save

chunk_findings.detail: `test_accuracy_knob_is_validated` does not actually validate the accuracy knob. It calls the private `_share` helper for invalid values (`-0.1` and `1.5`) and asserts that the result is truthy. For a value like `-0.1`, a correct validator for `swarm.conformance_min_accuracy` must reject it (raise or return a falsy/clamped value); the current test will either error/assert-fail, or pass only if `_share` accepts/returns something truthy for invalid input, giving false assurance that the knob is validated. The test should assert rejection (e.g. `pytest.raises(ValueError)` or that `Config` rejects the value), not truthiness.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_conformance.py:244

chunk_findings.detail: `_shown` accepts a gate call with an empty/missing action as a successful lease action (`("gate", ("", "record"))`). If the `gate_record` outcome requires `action="record"` (as the fixed gate-record tests imply), a stub lane can emit `claim`, `heartbeat`, a no-action `gate`, and enough other tool calls to satisfy `p.min_calls`; `_shown` then returns true and collection stops before the lane’s later `gate` call with `action="record"` is recorded. `grade` consequently sees no successful gate record and marks `gate_record` unavailable/failed, so the lane is denied the gate-record level even though it would have produced the required record if collection had continued.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:_shown

chunk_findings.detail: `save()` assumes `raw["lanes"]` is either falsy or a mapping. If the file is valid JSON with the current schema but `lanes` is a non-mapping, e.g. `{"schema": "lane-levels@1", "lanes": ["lane-a"]}`, then `lanes = dict(raw.get("lanes") or {})` raises `ValueError` (for a scalar it would raise `TypeError`) instead of treating the file as having no readable lanes or refusing it. `_reports()` would return `{}` for that document, and the previous `save()` path via `load_all()` would not crash here; now a scheduler/conformance save can fail on a corrupt-but-valid-JSON local file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance_io.py:save

chunk_findings.detail: The added `late` stub mode waits indefinitely with `while not os.path.exists(flag): time.sleep(0.05)`, while the other non-`once` stub mode has a bounded 20-second loop. If the flag file is not created or is removed before the stub observes it—for example, if the revocation/lease-stop step in `test_collection_waits_for_successful_lease_calls` is not reached because the lease path returns unavailable—the stub child never prints its late calls and never exits, so the test hangs until an external timeout instead of producing a failed/unavailable result. Direct invocation of the stub with `mode="late"` and a nonexistent flag path demonstrates the hang.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_conformance.py:39

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named for “a gate call for another action,” but it never supplies a gate call. `grade_calls(["claim", "heartbeat"], action="list")` produces only `claim` and `heartbeat` events, so `gate_record == FAILED` is true simply because no gate event exists. chunk_findings.detail: The helper used by the accuracy tests does not construct a valid gate-record call, yet the tests assert a level beyond gate-record. `grade_calls(base + ["bash"] * 2)` and `grade_calls(["claim", "heartbeat", "gate"] + ["bash"] * 2)` include a call named `gate` but omit `action="record"`, while asserting `level == 6`, i.e. after gate-record/hook/lease-stop have passed. If gate-record requires `action="record"` (as the `GOOD` script and the other test’s name imply), those reports cannot legitimately reach level 6. chunk_findings.detail: `_shown` accepts a gate call with an empty/missing action as a successful lease action (`("gate", ("", "record"))`). If the `gate_record` outcome requires `action="record"` (as the fixed gate-record tests imply), a stub lane can emit `claim`, `heartbeat`, a no-action `gate`, and enough other tool calls to satisfy `p.min_calls`; `_shown` then returns true and collection stops before the lane’s later `gate` call with `action="record"` is recorded. `grade` consequently sees no successful gate record and marks `gate_record` unavailable/failed, so the lane is denied the gate-record level even though it would have produced the required record if collection had continued.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:_shown

chunk_findings.detail: `save()` assumes `raw["lanes"]` is either falsy or a mapping. If the file is valid JSON with the current schema but `lanes` is a non-mapping, e.g. `{"schema": "lane-levels@1", "lanes": ["lane-a"]}`, then `lanes = dict(raw.get("lanes") or {})` raises `ValueError` (for a scalar it would raise `TypeError`) instead of treating the file as having no readable lanes or refusing it. `_reports()` would return `{}` for that document, and the previous `save()` path via `load_all()` would not crash here; now a scheduler/conformance save can fail on a corrupt-but-valid-JSON local file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance_io.py:save

chunk_findings.detail: The added `late` stub mode waits indefinitely with `while not os.path.exists(flag): time.sleep(0.05)`, while the other non-`once` stub mode has a bounded 20-second loop. If the flag file is not created or is removed before the stub observes it—for example, if the revocation/lease-stop step in `test_collection_waits_for_successful_lease_calls` is not reached because the lease path returns unavailable—the stub child never prints its late calls and never exits, so the test hangs until an external timeout instead of producing a failed/unavailable result. Direct invocation of the stub with `mode="late"` and a nonexistent flag path demonstrates the hang.

chunk_findings.detail: The `late` stub now bounds its wait with `end = time.time() + 20`, but it still prints the late `claim` and `heartbeat` calls unconditionally after the loop. If the revocation flag is never created, or is created after the 20-second timeout, the loop exits by timeout and the stub emits the same “late” events anyway. chunk_findings.detail: The knob is checked with `_count`, which permits `0`. If an operator sets `swarm.conformance_min_calls = 0`, then a conformance run that observes zero tool calls is not “fewer” than the minimum, so the documented “fewer is `unavailable`, never passed” gate is disabled and the run proceeds to judge accuracy on zero calls. That either makes the accuracy computation invalid (division by zero if not guarded) or allows an empty run to be treated as available/passed, contradicting the intent that “unavailable is not passed.” The minimum call count should be validated as positive, or the zero-call case must be forced unavailable before accuracy is judged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/swarm.py (`conformance_min_calls`)

chunk_findings.detail: `grade` treats launch as passed unless `stopped_clean` is explicitly `False`. It passes when `stopped_clean` is `None`, and `observe` sets `stopped_clean = driver.stop(h).status != "failed"`, so a stop result with status `"unavailable"` is also treated as clean. For example, `grade("lane", Observed(started=True), Params())` returns `launch` passed and `level=1` even though no clean stop was observed. In a live run, if `driver.stop(h)` returns `Result(status="unavailable", ...)`, the lane is graded as having stopped cleanly, contrary to the stated rule that unavailable is not passed and launch requires a clean stop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:grade/observe

chunk_findings.detail: `admits` converts a string `needed` level with `LEVEL_NAMES.index(needed)`, so an unknown level name raises `ValueError` instead of denying admission. For example, `admits(Report("lane", 5, (), 0.0), "hook_fire", Params())` crashes with `ValueError: 'hook_fire' is not in tuple`. A scheduler or config typo such as `"hook_fire"` for `"hook"` therefore takes down the admission check rather than returning `False`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:admits

chunk_findings.detail: `norm_tool` strips prefixes only in the order they appear in `_PREFIXES`, so it fails to strip a generic prefix after `ddflow.` or a repeated `ddflow_` prefix. For example, `norm_tool("ddflow.ddflow_claim")` returns `ddflow_claim`, not `claim`, and `norm_tool("ddflow_ddflow_claim")` also returns `ddflow_claim`. A stub endpoint or tool event using such a name will not match `_called(..., "claim")` or normalized `Params.tools` entries for `claim`, so the claim check or tool accuracy can fail even though the lane called the claim tool.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/conformance.py:norm_tool

chunk_findings.detail: `save()` is not safe for concurrent updates even though the final `os.replace()` is atomic. It performs a non-atomic read-modify-write: `load_all()` reads the current lane set, then the new lane is added and the whole file is replaced. If two processes (or threads in one process) call `save()` for different lanes, both can read the same prior state before either writes. For example, starting from no lane levels, process A calls `save(lane_a)`, process B calls `save(lane_b)`, and the interleaving is A load, B load, A replace, B replace. The final file contains only `lane_b`, silently erasing `lane_a`’s conformance level even though it passed. This can leave a lane unadmitted despite a recorded pass.

chunk_findings.detail: `load_all()` treats any schema other than `lane-levels@1` as if there are no lanes, and `save()` then uses that empty result to overwrite the file with schema `lane-levels@1`. If the file is written by a newer version, e.g. `.ddflow/local/lane-levels.json` contains `{"schema": "lane-levels@2", "lanes": {"lane-a": ...}}`, then `load_all()` returns `{}`. A subsequent `save(report)` for `lane-b` writes a new file containing only `lane-b` under `lane-levels@1`, deleting all other lanes and downgrading the schema. An unknown/new schema should be rejected or preserved, not silently clobbered.

chunk_findings.detail: The `late` stub now suppresses all late calls when the revocation flag is absent.
